newsitem.title: UK: Options -- Gold OTC vols tick up but business thin.
newsitem.headline: Options -- Gold OTC vols tick up but business thin.

text.p: Business has been relatively dull in gold OTC options, despite the brief venture of the spot price below $380 and a subsequent uptick in near-term volatilities, dealers said.
Volatilities have firmed by about a quarter to half a percentage point, mostly in the one- to three-month dates, they added.
"The puts came up half a point, slightly higher than for the calls at first, but now it's about the same for calls and puts," one dealer said.
"There were some puts between $370 and $380 which came into the game, which were bought," he added.
Since out-of-the money puts such as $375 have been bid up, people were gravitating to strikes closer to the market, another said.
"People are not keen to buy such expensive volatility when they can buy at-the-money much lower," he added.

Now that spot prices have settled back around $380, fears of producer hedging have led to interest in the puts while investors see this as a good level to purchase out-of-the-money calls, another dealer said.
Over the past few days, dealers have seen some selling of out-of-the money November and December calls between $382-$390.
"I think there are some customers trying to cash in some premiums. I think people are rather comfortable losing calls between $384 and $387," a dealer in continental Europe said.
Another dealer said: "Today I saw a good offer of 5.7 (percent) on a $385 call for December but nothing really different than what we have seen over the past few days, nothing huge."
Gold at-the-money implied volatilities for October were bid at 4.6 to 5.0 percent, December at 5.30 percent, March at 5.6 to 6.00 percent and one year at 6.6 to 6.9 percent.
Volumes have increased since the summer lull, but were still at relatively low levels, dealers said.

"It's been really quiet for one week now. Most of the interest in the market is focused on the forwards. If you trade both options and forwards you are much busier on the forwards these days," one said.
The silver options market was lacklustre, dealers said.
"It has not created any activity below $5.00. Silver is a non-event for the time being," one said.
